title: Stanford benchmark scores agents as teammates
summary: The Collaborative Intelligence Benchmark has 240 tasks across 8 teamwork skills drawn from real records. The best of 18 models scores 82.2 out of 100, and every model loses 20 to 47 points when a teammate creates a problem. 160 tasks are public with code and data.

appearances.summary: New paper testing AI models as collaborators rather than solo solvers. Across 18 models and 240 tasks the top score was 82.2 of 100. Frontier models almost never cheat, but they tend to give in when a teammate pushes back, which matters for multi-agent and human-in-the-loop setups.
